title: UTF-8 safe text
description:
Write four functions that treat text as characters, not bytes, so they work for any language:

```lua-norun
char_count(s)        -- the number of characters in the UTF-8 text s
reverse_text(s)      -- s with its characters in the opposite order (not its bytes)
truncate(s, n)       -- the first n characters of s followed by "…" when s has more than n characters; s itself otherwise
is_ascii(s)          -- true when every byte of s is below 128
```

```lua-norun
char_count("café")          --> 4   (#"café" is 5)
reverse_text("añb")         --> "bña"
truncate("crème brûlée", 5) --> "crème…"
```
hints: `utf8.charpattern` matches one character; `s:gmatch(utf8.charpattern)` gives them one by one.
`utf8.offset(s, n + 1)` is the byte where character n + 1 starts, so the first n characters end one byte before it.
unitTests:
test("counting characters", function()
    check_eq(char_count("café"), 4)
    check_eq(char_count("hello"), 5)
    check_eq(char_count("€😀"), 2)
    check_eq(char_count(""), 0)
end)

test("reversing characters", function()
    check_eq(reverse_text("añb"), "bña")
    check_eq(reverse_text("lua"), "aul")
    check_eq(reverse_text("¡Olé!"), "!élO¡")
    check_eq(reverse_text(""), "")
end)

test("truncating", function()
    check_eq(truncate("crème brûlée", 5), "crème…")
    check_eq(truncate("short", 10), "short")
    check_eq(truncate("exact", 5), "exact")
    check_eq(truncate("日本語のテキスト", 3), "日本語…")
end)

test("ascii", function()
    check(is_ascii("plain text 123"), "plain text")
    check(not is_ascii("café"), "café")
    check(is_ascii(""), "the empty string")
end)
